name: Marl & Cane
oneLiner: A single-vineyard estate whose page is one year of one bunch: eighty-one scrubbed frames of veraison, the fruit turning green to black under the reader's scroll, and the laboratory record that decided the picking date.

axes.secondaryReason: the spec left D's secondary an open draw between physics-interaction and brutalist-raw, and the motion budget decided it: physics would have been a SECOND motion system competing with the scroll spine for one clock (Morningside's argument, reused because it is correct), while brutalist-raw costs zero motion budget because it lives in structure, type and the flat presentation of numbers. It is also the sharpest refusal of what the look-first sweep found the category defaults to — oxblood, gilt rules and a centred Didone selling a bottle — and concrete is a real winery material rather than a conceit. The founder's own counterweight rule is satisfied structurally: the page's entire hero is a living plant in raking sunlight, so brutalism is the frame around the nature and never the subject
axes.portfolioNew: checked against all 24 shipped site.json files in both orderings — no site pairs otherworldly-animation with brutalist-raw, and the unordered set {otherworldly, brutalist} appears nowhere

paletteSeed: an ACHROMATIC page holding exactly one chromatic event — bone (#ede9e1) ground, near-black ink, and a single accent that walks with the scrub because its HUE is measured off the frames the scrub is showing (68° yellow-green at the unripe bunch, 40° as it turns, 4° red as it darkens). Deliberately the opposite move to small-hours, which also derives its colour from its instrument but drenches the whole page in it; here the world stays resolutely grey and the fruit is the only thing in it allowed to have a colour. The accent's LIGHTNESS is solved per hue for a constant 4.85:1 against bone rather than fixed, because a fixed lightness across a hue sweep fails AA at the green end — measured, 29 of 81 frames failed before the fix. The final purple is a stated design choice, not a measurement: by the last frames the fruit is too desaturated for a hue to be meaningful, and /guide says so
typeDirection: Syne (variable) for display — a contemporary, slightly strange face with an art-institution register rather than a winery one, chosen to refuse the high-contrast Didone the vertical defaults to — against Geist and Geist Mono for everything the estate states as fact: the vintage figures, the chapter marks, the ripening table and the chart's ticks. The mono is the deliberate inversion of Morningside's 'no monospace' rule and for the same underlying reason: that page's differentiation was NOT being an instrument, and this one's is that it carries a laboratory record. All three OFL, all three portfolio-new, all vendored locally
motionBudget: ONE scroll clock and no second animation system: 81 scrubbed frames of a single 8s Seedance take, one bunch of Cabernet going green to blue-black through veraison, driven by four chapter anchors (0 · 20 · 44 · 80) whose spans are DERIVED from the frames each drives at 46px/frame desktop and 26px/frame touch. Each chapter's anchor is its BOTTOM edge, so the turn happens while the turn is being read. The take's live range was MEASURED, not assumed: the fruit stops changing at native frame ~126 and the last ~65 frames are one still picture, so the manifest ships range [0,126] and the dead third is never spent on scroll. The stage is bounded on VIEWPORT HEIGHT as well as width so it cannot outgrow a short laptop window, and the page deliberately ENDS its motion before it ends its argument — chapter four says the picture stops changing, because it does, and the last five weeks of the vintage happen only in the numbers. Reduced-motion gets discrete states rather than interpolation; no-JS gets the full chart, table, every chapter and one lit frame

verdict.note: Site D of the landing arc (docs/landing-arc/spec.md) and the LAST site in the arc. Named Marl & Cane after the spec's own collision check failed on 'Veraison' — multiple live trading names, a near-homophone winery and a registered trademark holder — while marl (a clay-limestone vineyard soil) and cane (the one-year wood cane-pruning leaves) are both real viticulture and collide with nothing. The name and the page argue opposite halves of the same idea on purpose: the masthead holds the two constants, the page is about the one year that never repeats, which is also how it differentiates from orchard-house's repeating cycle. The spec's ~110cr three-segment tier is SUPERSEDED by s107/s108: veraison is a one-way transformation of a single subject, so it is ONE take, and the spine cost 36cr rather than ~110. Ships a LIGHT instrument, the opposite call to Morningside's none — nothing in the portfolio plots ripeness, the Brix/acid curve is what the discipline itself produces, and its lay twin is free and unusually honest because veraison IS the visible proxy for sugar accumulation: the curve carries the evidence and the fruit's colour carries the feeling, two readings of one physical process on one clock.
